paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: when the LORD of Hosts swears something, it's done. He says, "Surely, as I have planned, so will it be; as I have purposed, so will it stand." (Isaiah 14:24) That's not a maybe. That's an oath, and nobody has to wonder if the dough will rise.

Now look at who stood in the way. Assyria was the empire that carried Israel away (2 Kings 17:6), and the LORD says, "His yoke will be taken off My people, and his burden removed from their shoulders." (Isaiah 14:25) The heavy thing on His people was never too heavy for Him. Whatever feels like it's sitting on your shoulders right now, I want you to hear that, baker.

Then the passage ends with two questions: "who can thwart Him?" and "who can turn it back?" (Isaiah 14:27) The answer is NO ONE, and I think that's the most comforting sentence in the whole bakery. My plans change every time the timer goes off, but His plan is "for the whole earth" (Isaiah 14:26) and it stands. So you can rest your whole weight on Him, friend.
